title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the description of sections of the group scheme \hat G_{ρ,σ}, the 'Galois-type' extension attached to a pair ρ,σ in GL(2) in the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' cycle. The previous page set up the question: given β and a sign ε, when can one complete them to a section (α,β,μ,ε)? Here σ(·) and ρ(·) denote the twisted (conjugation) actions.

Step 1. Write βσ(β)^{-1} = (R0 S0; T0 U0). A necessary condition for completing (β,ε) is that U0 be invertible. This condition depends only on β, not on ε.

Step 2. Assume U0 is invertible. Choose ε arbitrarily among the sign sections (Γ(μ_2), i.e. ±1 locally). Then η = ε·βσ(β)^{-1} is a section of the subscheme A_σ ⊂ G of solutions of det η = 1, Tr(ησ) = Tr(σ). This is the lemma of p. 455.

Step 3. By the theorem of part (II), set μ = 1/U = ε/U0, where U is the lower-right entry of η.

Step 4. Define ξ = η·ε1^{μ-1}. Here ε1 = ρσ^{-1} is the regular unipotent, and ε1^{μ-1} is its unipotent power with exponent μ-1.

Step 5. ξ can then be written locally as αρ(α)^{-1}. This is a twisted-conjugacy (Lang-map / nonabelian H^1) statement. The indeterminacy is right multiplication α ↦ αb by sections b of the centralizer torus T_ρ, so the fibre is a T_ρ-torsor.

Conclusion. For fixed β, μ can only take the two values ε/U0 with ε = ±1. This answers the remark on the previous page: β alone does not determine μ, but (β,ε) does.

The next page begins part (VI), the characterisation of 'modular' triples (ε1,ρ,σ) over a general base S, using Azumaya algebras and P^1-bundles. So this page is a technical lemma in a local parametrisation of these torsor-like schemes.
errors: The transcription '(elle ne dépend que de β, μ et ε)' contradicts the logic, since U0 is defined from β alone. The manuscript most likely reads '(elle ne dépend que de β, pas de ε)'.
'μ = 1/U = ε/(U0σ)' carries a stray 'σ'. It should be μ = 1/U = ε/U0, consistent with formula (42) of the previous page. U = ε·U0 because η = ε·βσ(β)^{-1}.

The local solvability of ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} is asserted 'loc.t' (locally) without proof here. It presumably rests on the theorem of (II) and on T_ρ being smooth, so that torsors are locally trivial in the étale or fppf topology. Over a general base this is local, not global; Grothendieck correctly notes 'loc.t'.
